units.translation: Aristophanes Frogs 1478 makes Aeschylus say οὐ χρὴ λέοντος σκύμνον ἐν πόλει τρέφειν [one must not rear a lion's whelp in the city]. From this it does not follow that Aeschylus used this verse in some tragedy.

There are two forms of this adjective, μικρός [small] and σμικρός [small], which the scenic poets preferred in such a way that they used them only for the sake of meter or euphony: the scribes preserved this rule fairly consistently. μικρός [small] is read in Sophocles in three places when the meter demands it, never in Aeschylus, whose examples all admit either form, with one exception, Ch. 262, where the meter demands ἀπὸ σμικροῦ [from a small one].
